title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattentionv2 + fused ops + rope/rotary optimizations
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: reduce tail latency and improve throughput across common workload distributions by upgrading attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 and introducing fused rotary/rope operations. This PR adds optimized CUDA kernels, a kernel selection path in the runtime scheduler, and a redesigned KV cache layout to support fused ops with contiguous memory for better bandwidth utilization.

Summary of changes (high-level): added native FlashAttentionV2 kernels with heuristics for choosing fast paths; implemented fused rotary/rope application inside the attention kernel to avoid extra memory traffic; refactored KV cache layout to store per-head contiguous K/V blocks to enable single-copy cache hot paths; extended kernel selector to factor in sequence length, batch size, and quantization mode; added microbenchmarks and end-to-end perf tests; documented behavior and rollback steps.

Checklist: [x] FlashAttentionV2 kernels implemented and unit-tested on CUDA 11/12; [x] fused rope/rotary ops implemented and validated against reference outputs; [x] KV cache backward-compatible on-disk/serialization layout with migration helpers; [x] scheduler heuristics added with feature flag to enable rollout; [x] perf harnesses added and benchmarks collected on internal hardware pool; [x] docs + release notes drafted.

Rollout plan: enable behind runtime flag attn_v2_fused by default for new deployments; gradual ramp on Dedicated pools with canary percentiles; monitor cost/perf dashboards and automatically rollback if p99 latency regresses >10% vs baseline.

Notes: kept CPU fallback path unchanged (calls existing CPU attention) to reduce risk for non-GPU customers. Known limitations: a very small subset of old quantized kernels (int4 custom path) falls back to slower path until separate quantization-optimized kernels are added next quarter.

release_notes: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope ops. Performance improvements across short and medium sequence lengths, reduced per-token cost through kernel fusion and KV cache layout optimizations. Feature gated rollout with automatic rollback on regressions.
performance_summary: Short sequences (<=128): p99 latency -45%, Medium (512): p99 latency -28%, Long (2048): p99 latency -6%. Throughput +15% average across models tested. GPU memory usage reduced ~8% for typical batch sizes due to contiguous KV layout and reduced temp buffers.
testing_summary: Accuracy tests cover fused-rotary outputs vs reference CPU implementation across FP16/FP32 and FP16+quantized-hot paths. Microbench harness runs on 8xA100 (40GB) and internal small-GPU pool for regression checks. End-to-end tests exercise serving pipeline including KV cache migration path.
rollback_plan: Disable runtime flag attn_v2_fused via control plane will immediately route new requests to legacy kernels; mature Dedicated pools will be rolled back via canary policy. KV cache migration is reversible - migration step creates versioned cache files and a fallback reader. Monitor p99/p50 and error-rate dashboards during rollback.
notes: This change is non-breaking for API consumers. Customers with extremely tight quantized int4 paths may see a temporary fallback to slower path until quantization-optimized kernels are added.
